{{Short description|Construction in combinatorial group theory}}
In the area of [[mathematics]] called [[combinatorial group theory]], the '''Schreier coset graph''' is a [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graph]] associated with a [[group (mathematics)|group]] ''G'', a [[Generating set of a group|generating set]] of ''G'', and a [[subgroup]] of ''G''. The Schreier graph encodes the abstract structure of the group modulo an [[equivalence relation]] formed by the [[coset]]s of the subgroup.

The graph is named after [[Otto Schreier]], who used the term "{{lang|de|Nebengruppenbild}}".<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Otto |last1=Schreier |title=Die Untergruppen der freien Gruppen |journal=Abhandlungen aus dem Mathematischen Seminar der Universität Hamburg |volume=5 |issue=1 |date=December 1927 |pages=161–183 |doi=10.1007/BF02952517}}</ref> An equivalent definition [[Todd–Coxeter algorithm|was made]] in an early paper of Todd and Coxeter.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=J.A. |last1=Todd |author-link=J. A. Todd |first2=H.S.M. |last2=Coxeter |author2-link=H. S. M. Coxeter |title=A practical method for enumerating cosets of a finite abstract group |journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society |volume=5 |issue=1 |date=October 1936 |pages=26–34 |doi=10.1017/S0013091500008221 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Description==
Given a group ''G'', a subgroup ''H'' ≤ ''G'', and a generating set ''S'' = {''s''<sub>''i''</sub>: ''i'' in ''I''} of ''G'', the Schreier graph Sch(''G'', ''H'', ''S'') is a graph whose [[vertex (graph theory)|vertices]] are the right [[coset]]s ''Hg'' = {''hg'': ''h'' in ''H''} for ''g'' in ''G'' and whose [[edge (graph theory)|edges]] are of the form (''Hg'', ''Hgs'') for ''g'' in ''G'' and ''s'' in ''S''.   

More generally, if ''X'' is any [[G-set|''G''-set]], one can define a Schreier graph Sch(''G'', ''X'', ''S'') of the [[Group action|action]] of ''G'' on ''X'' (with respect to the generating set ''S''): its vertices are the elements of ''X'', and its edges are of the form (''x'', ''xs'') for ''x'' in ''X'' and ''s'' in ''S''. This includes the original Schreier coset graph definition, as ''H''\''G'' is a naturally a ''G''-set with respect to multiplication from the right. From an [[Algebraic topology|algebraic-topological]] perspective, the graph Sch(''G'', ''X'', ''S'') has no distinguished vertex, whereas Sch(''G'', ''H'', ''S'') has the distinguished vertex ''H'', and is thus a [[Pointed space|pointed graph]].  

The [[Cayley graph]] of the group ''G'' itself is the Schreier coset graph for ''H'' = {1<sub>''G''</sub>}.<ref>{{Citation |last1=Gross |first1=Jonathan L. |title=Topological graph theory |page=73 |year=1987 |series=Wiley-Interscience Series in Discrete Mathematics and Optimization |location=New York |publisher=[[John Wiley & Sons]] |isbn=978-0-471-04926-5 |mr=898434 |last2=Tucker |first2=Thomas W.}}</ref>  

A [[spanning tree]] of a Schreier coset graph corresponds to a Schreier transversal, as in [[Schreier's subgroup lemma]].<ref name=":0">{{Citation |last1=Conder |first1=Marston |title=Groups St. Andrews 2001 in Oxford. Vol. I |volume=304 |pages=63–91 |year=2003 |series=London Math. Soc. Lecture Note Ser. |chapter=Group actions on graphs, maps and surfaces with maximum symmetry |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |mr=2051519 |authorlink=Marston Conder}}</ref>

The book "Categories and Groupoids" listed below relates this to the theory of covering morphisms of [[groupoid]]s. A subgroup ''H'' of a group ''G'' determines a covering morphism of groupoids <math> p: K \rightarrow G </math>  and if ''S'' is a generating set for ''G'' then its [[inverse image]] under ''p'' is the Schreier graph of (''G'', ''S'').

==Applications==
The graph is useful to understand [[coset enumeration]] and the [[Todd–Coxeter algorithm]].  

Coset graphs can be used to form large [[permutation representation]]s of groups and were used by [[Graham Higman]] to show that the [[alternating group]]s of large enough degree are [[Hurwitz group]]s.<ref name=":0" />

[[John R. Stallings|Stallings]]' core graphs<ref>John R. Stallings. [[doi:10.1007/BF02095993|"Topology of finite graphs."]] ''[[Inventiones Mathematicae]]'', vol. 71  (1983),  no. 3, pp. 551–565</ref> are [[Retraction (topology)|retracts]] of Schreier graphs of free groups, and are an essential tool for computing with subgroups of a free group.

Every [[vertex-transitive graph]] is a coset graph.
